notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null; no human reviewed or tested this package and no hardware run happened. Only the fake backend is declared. The card names upstream-sim (Isaac Gym), but Isaac Gym Preview 4 is a manual download from NVIDIA (README.md:22-24) and was neither installed nor imported; fake.py is a pure Python single-environment stand-in for DexHandBase. The deployed fake is kinematic, so the fidelity contract says F0, engine analytic:dexhand021-fake, timestep 5.0 ms (the configured physics timestep, BaseTask.yaml:10), realtime_factor 0, lockstep clock, full reset and snapshot_restore false; the gaps list what is not modelled (no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, contact forces, PD actuators, tendon coupling, sensor noise, rendering, or the runtime-measured control period, and the 5 contact indicators stay zero). The fake was never compared with an Isaac Gym run, no physical DexHand is modelled, and the 224-value observation is one flat row of the upstream batched buffer. The only warnings are expected for the Gymnasium family and were not cleared: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it records the seed for the next reset and makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived integer inputs and the action.values numbers (reset seed, seed action seed, step ticks, step action.values); the action limit is derived by the bridge from the fake action space (FakeDexHandBase:action_space) and is not an upstream Fact or Limit. Only the catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue requests. The only stop is the runtime's software latch (simulated R0); there is no hardware backend. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package. gate.digest is the digest the last check printed.
